LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 INTERROGATIVES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives, part of Strand 11 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: why, which, whisper, where and whole, • practise using when clauses with present tense to show the future, for example, ‘When are you going to school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss in pairs or groups

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss in pairs or groups

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: The learner’s ability to clearly communicate with others is improved as they use clauses with

present tense to show the future.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner’s ability to come up with new ideas is enhanced as they create lists of

interrogative sentences using words related to the theme.

Values:
Responsibility: This is inculcated in the learner as they engage in assigned tasks and collaborate with peers to use

interrogatives in sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills: Self-esteem is nurtured as the learner practises using interrogatives in sentences.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of interrogatives to their learning in Kiswahili.
